scope: Isolated native-style one-level traversal and alternative projection/cavity experiments on three pinned Split controls.
method: Use a one-level native-style octant order, preserve application segment order and perform exact-incircle cavity insertion. Compare the current barycentric metric, an orthonormalized face metric, and affine frames reconstructed from the three captured native corner projections. Count unordered output facet multiset matches.
staticObservation: The retained per-face native routine builds and inverts a local frame, casts projected values and per-axis scale denominators through Float32, and normalizes the two axes independently. The two static helper decompilations are retained for further analysis; exact signatures and general behavior remain to be verified.
limitations: The captured-frame variant injects native oracle data for each face; it is not a general implementation or independent validation.
The native-style tree is only one level and has no general subdivision implementation.
The result does not establish arbitrary input behavior, constraints, performance, public MCP or GUI lifecycle.
Facet counts compare unordered geometry, not orientation, normals or native object lifecycle.
No candidate was applied to the application.
